newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities lower heading into the weekend.
newsitem.headline: German equities lower heading into the weekend.

text.p: The IBIS DAX traded just shy of 3,000 points on Friday, with the market still suffering from an overnight correction on Wall Street, with no new good news evident in early trade across the Atlantic to lift the market.

At 1513 GMT the IBIS DAX index stood at 2,997.47 points, not far off the psychologically-important 3,000-point level, but seemingly unable to convincingly penetrate that threshold and forge further gains.
"We would welcome a bit of a breather in this market after the last couple of weeks, but we are mostly looking to new data next week to decide where we'll go," said one Frankfurt trader.
The Dow Jones Industrial Index opened slightly lower, but inconclusively so, and the German market could not take any direction from early trade on Wall Street.
Support came from the dollar at 1.6278/84 marks, off the highs of earlier in the week, but still stable enough to underpin trade.
Traders said that many shares saw a lot of volatility over the day, including Mannesmann AG, which was down 10.40 marks at 642.80 marks in afternoon trade.
Focus was also on the banking sector, in favour of late, especially Bayerische Hypotheken-und Wechselbank.
Hypo-Bank was up 1.20 marks, or 2.28 percent, at 53.85 marks, amid speculation that it was trying to dispose of some of its industrial holdings.
Next week's corporate events include annual results from Thyssen AG in Duesseldorf on Monday, and dealers said they were expecting positive developments in Thyssen's earnings per share for 1996.
